title: Non-coding genetic variants underlying higher prostate cancer risk in men of African ancestry.
authors: Li, Shan; Fatema, Kaniz; Nidharshan, Sundarraj; Singh, Arashdeep; Rajagopal, Padma Sheila; Notani, Dimple; Takeda, David; Hannenhalli, Sridhar
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
one_liner_zh: 该文用序列深度学习模型识别非洲裔男性前列腺癌风险相关非编码增强子SNP，并实验验证其影响转录因子结合，虽涉及TF-DNA结合位点预测但非核心建模机制，方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作研究。
abstract: Incidence and severity of prostate cancer (PrCa) substantially varies across ancestries. American men of African ancestry (AA) are more likely to be diagnosed with and die from PrCa than the those of European ancestry (EA). Published polygenic risk scores for developing prostate cancer, even those based on multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies, do not address population-specific genetic mechanisms underlying PrCa risk in men of African ancestry. Specifically, the role of non-coding regulatory polymorphisms in driving inter-ancestry variation in PrCa has not been sufficiently explored. Here, by employing a sequence-based deep learning model of prostate regulatory enhancers, we identified ~2,000 SNPs with higher alternate allele frequency in AA men that potentially affect enhancer function associated with PrCa susceptibility, as supported by our experimental validation. The identified enhancer SNPs (eSNPs) may influence PrCa development through two complementary mechanisms: 1) the alternate allele that increase enhancer activity result in immune suppression and telomere elongation, and 2) the alternate alleles that decrease enhancer activity, lead to de-differentiation and inhibition of apoptosis. Notably, the eSNPs tend to disrupt the binding of known prostate transcription factors including FOX, AR and HOX families. Lastly, the identified eSNPs can be combined into a polygenic risk score that adds value to current GWAS-based risk variants in assessing PrCa risk in independent cohorts.
abstract_zh: 前列腺癌（PrCa）的发病率和严重程度在不同祖先群体间存在显著差异。非洲裔美国男性（AA）比欧洲裔美国男性（EA）更易被诊断出患有PrCa并因此死亡。已发表的前列腺癌多基因风险评分，即使是基于多祖先全基因组关联研究，也未解决非洲裔男性中PrCa风险背后的群体特异性遗传机制。具体而言，非编码调控多态性在驱动PrCa跨祖先差异中的作用尚未得到充分探索。在此，通过采用基于序列的前列腺调控增强子深度学习模型，我们识别出约2,000个在AA男性中具有较高替代等位基因频率的SNP，这些SNP可能影响与PrCa易感性相关的增强子功能，并得到我们实验验证的支持。所识别的增强子SNP（eSNPs）可能通过两种互补机制影响PrCa发展：1）增加增强子活性的替代等位基因导致免疫抑制和端粒延长，以及2）降低增强子活性的替代等位基因导致去分化和凋亡抑制。值得注意的是，eSNPs倾向于破坏已知前列腺转录因子（包括FOX、AR和HOX家族）的结合。最后，所识别的eSNPs可组合成多基因风险评分，在独立队列中评估PrCa风险时，为当前基于GWAS的风险变异增添价值。
